subject: Post-discovery: evaluation sprint plan & scheduling
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Kate Liu <kate.liu@finzen.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Nov 2025 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Post-discovery: evaluation sprint plan & scheduling

Kate — thanks again for the conversation this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same view: 

Summary from discovery:
- Primary use case: customer support summarization + semantic search over policy docs (~200k documents).
- Success criteria: 95% intent match on a 200-sample prompt set, avg generation latency < 350ms P95 for 1–2k concurrent users.
- Constraints: data residency for sensitive artifacts (US only), SOC 2 evidence required by procurement.

Proposed evaluation plan (30–45 day sprint):
1) Week 0: kickoff — align on success criteria, share sample prompt set, technical constraints, and baseline metrics.
2) Week 1–2: ingest sample prompts & data subset, run initial quality checks.
3) Week 3–4: iterate on prompt templates, measure latency/cost, run final acceptance evals.

Next meeting ask: schedule an evaluation kickoff (business sync + technical deep dive). Suggested windows (PST):
- Thu Dec 3, 10:00–11:00 (business sync)
- Fri Dec 4, 11:00–12:30 (technical deep dive, SE + infra deep dive)

Attachments: evaluation-scope.pdf (proposed milestones) and sample-prompt-set.csv (redacted).

If those windows don't work, please share up to three alternatives and we'll align. Marissa will coordinate commercial details; Dev will lead the tech deep dive.

Thanks — Sergio
Sergio Alvarez | Senior Solutions Lead
Redwood Inference
sergio@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

From: Kate Liu <kate.liu@finzen.com>

Cc: FinZen Procurement <procurement@finzen.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Nov 2025 11:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-discovery: evaluation sprint plan & scheduling

Thanks, Sergio — helpful recap. We are definitely aligned on the high-level goals. A few notes from our side: 

- Success criteria: we will formalize the 200-sample prompt set and share it by end of week. In addition to intent match, our product team will evaluate hallucination rate on NER-sensitive prompts.
- Latency: <350ms P95 is preferred but we'd be OK evaluating up to 450ms P95 if cost tradeoffs are reasonable.
- Procurement asks: SOC 2 Type II report + data processing addendum. They’ve asked for an initial pricing ballpark for a 30-day eval (including any reserved capacity needed).

Scheduling: Dec 3 at 10:00 PST works for our business sync. For the technical deep dive, Dec 4 at 11:00 PST is likely OK but I need to confirm with our infra lead (CCed procurement is just for procurement/contract questions).

Proposed attendees from FinZen: Kate Liu (PM), Andrew Cho (infra lead — tentative), Procurement mailbox.

Appreciate the attachments — I’ll review and return comments by Wednesday.

Best,
Kate

Kate — great, glad Dec 3 works. Quick notes from commercial/ops: 

- I'll send a short evaluation statement of work and a preliminary pricing worksheet tomorrow (includes an option for a 30-day reserved capacity (small) vs. on-demand).
- For procurement: we can share SOC 2 evidence and a standard DPA; attaching the eval scope now (see attachment). If procurement needs anything else, flag it and I’ll loop in Solutions + Legal.

On meeting format: I suggest we split the first block into two parts (same hour):
- 10:00–10:25: business goals & success criteria (PMs)
- 10:25–11:00: logistics & eval mechanics (SOW, timelines, data transfer specifics)

For the technical deep dive (Dev will lead): would be helpful to get answers to these beforehand:
- expected average document length and size distribution
- if you have a dev/test dataset we can use (S3 link or sanitized export)
- whether you expect any long-tail contextual sessions > 2048 tokens

I’ll send the calendar invite once we confirm times.

Thanks — Marissa

Thanks — quick note from the SE side: I can run a lightweight benchmarking harness during week 1 if you can provide:
- a 1k-sample of your typical user prompts and a 200-sample of high-risk prompts (the sample-prompt-set.csv helps).
- a small subset of anonymized documents (we only need ~5k docs to validate retrieval + summarization quality).

Pre-call checklist I’ll prepare:
- baseline quality run (redwood standard eval)
- target latency profiles for the model variants we propose
- cost estimate per 1k tokens at the expected concurrency

I’ll attach a short infra checklist (infra-checklist.md) to the invite and will be prepared to walk the FinZen infra lead through data ingestion options (S3, VPC peering).
